title: Veteran Actress Sowcar Janaki, 94, Hospitalized in Chennai; Undergoes ICU Treatment
excerpt: The Padma Shri-winning actress, who appeared in more than 450 films across seven decades of South Indian cinema, is reported to be in critical condition.
body:
• Veteran South Indian actress Sowcar Janaki, 94, has been hospitalized and is undergoing ICU treatment in Chennai
  • Multiple reports describe her condition as critical, with the actress receiving intensive medical care
  • Sowcar Janaki's career spans more than seven decades and over 450 films across Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Hindi cinema
  • She received the Padma Shri in 2022 in recognition of her contributions to Indian cinema

Veteran actress Sowcar Janaki has been hospitalized in Chennai and is undergoing treatment in the intensive care unit, according to multiple media reports from South Indian outlets. The 94-year-old actress, whose career in Indian cinema spans more than seven decades, is described as being in critical condition.

A Career Spanning Seven Decades

Sowcar Janaki — born Sankaramanchi Janaki on December 12, 1931 — is one of the last surviving links to the golden age of South Indian cinema. She earned her screen name from the 1950 Tamil film "Shavukaru" (meaning moneylender), directed by L.V. Prasad, a role that became so iconic that it became inseparable from her identity.

Over a career that began in the late 1940s and extended across more than 450 films, she worked in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Hindi cinema. Her filmography includes landmark productions such as "Parasakti" (1952), which starred Sivaji Ganesan and became a touchstone of the Dravidian movement in Tamil politics, and "Pava Mannippu" (1961). She was known for her ability to portray complex, emotionally demanding characters — often playing mother and authority figures in her later career after decades as a leading lady.

Recognition and Legacy

Sowcar Janaki received the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian honor, in 2022 for her decades of service to Indian cinema. She is among a small number of actresses from the early era of South Indian film who remained active across multiple languages and multiple generations of the industry.

Her career intersected with virtually every major figure in Tamil and Telugu cinema, from Sivaji Ganesan and M.G. Ramachandran to Rajinikanth and Kamal Haasan. She appeared in films directed by many of the industry's defining filmmakers, including K. Balachander, L.V. Prasad, and B.R. Panthulu.

Her hospitalization comes less than six weeks after the death of another towering figure in South Indian culture — legendary playback singer S. Janaki, who passed away in Mysuru on July 11, 2026, at the age of 88. Despite sharing a surname and an era, the two Janakis were unrelated and worked in entirely different domains of the film industry — one behind the microphone, the other in front of the camera.

An Industry Watches

News of Sowcar Janaki's hospitalization has drawn concern from across the Indian film industry. At 94, she represents a generation of performers whose careers predated both the New Wave and the commercial blockbuster era, bridging the studio system of the 1950s with the star-driven cinema that followed.

Further details about her medical condition have not been publicly disclosed. Reports from Gulte, Deccan Chronicle, The Indian Express, and The Times of India have confirmed the hospitalization, with CVR News in Telugu providing early video coverage. Her family has not issued a public statement as of the latest reports.

For the Indian diaspora — particularly South Indian communities in the United States, United Kingdom, and the Middle East — Sowcar Janaki's films are part of the cultural fabric that connected immigrant families to the cinema traditions of their home states. Her hospitalization has prompted an outpouring of concern and well-wishes on social media from fans around the world.
